limits: The later fused K64 candidate was rejected: its saved output hashes differed from the reference. It is not included.

The 21/23-bit K64 engines use the recorded general CRT source. Other single-precision sets combine that K64 arithmetic with the listed width tables; equality to the Arm libraries has not been checked.
Single-precision widths are the narrowest tried in the saved cases, not proven minimum widths. The SGEMM 23-bit nine-modulus choice uses the B300-selected table; there is no B200 timing claim for it.
The INT8 library retains FP16 comparison components to preserve its device build. The public C API selects the exact INT8 path only.
The INT8 implementation uses checked FP32 accumulation with an exact integer fallback. CRT coverage does not apply to that method.
The complex Level-3 accuracy record used a different Arm engine from the saved ZGEMM library. Correctness records for complex and real Level-3 are not timing records.
53-bit triangular solve timings and 57-bit accuracy checks are separate. 53-bit random-input accuracy did not always meet the native target. 57-bit checks cover only the listed fixed cases.

triangular_solve.hardware: One GB200 GPU, SM100, Arm; CUDA runtime 13030 and cuBLAS 13.8
triangular_solve.scope: Recorded prototype results. The 53-bit timing numbers do not apply to the 57-bit choice. The public frontend and its current source have not been run or timed on GPU.

timing.method: Median CPU wall time including encoding, CRT and synchronization, excluding creation, transfers and checks

single_general_crt_measurement.conditions: Uniform inputs, M=N=4096, K=1024 or 4096; four alternating old/new rounds, three warmups and twenty calls per round
single_general_crt_measurement.validation: All 32 output hashes, 32768 sampled values and 640 timing rows agreed with the independent check. This is not a new check of the public API.
single_general_crt_measurement.comparison_source: 21-bit rectangular GEMM and 23-bit SYRK from the recorded general CRT implementation
